basis: Neurodevelopmental disease; clubfoot in 1/2 reported patients is a functional skeletal deformity. Facial dysmorphism and central hypotonia do not add organs.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: clubfoot is a functionally important structural deformity in 1/2 patients; the small sample limits confidence.

basis: Kyphoscoliosis/joint instability define kEDS. Skin fragility/scarring and hypermetropia each occur in 30-79%; arterial events and hearing loss lack >=30% support.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: skin fragility and abnormal scarring occur in 30-79%; they are additional manifestations, whereas the defining kEDS criteria are musculoskeletal.

basis: Usually autoimmune anterior pituitary inflammation with hormone deficiency. Chiasmal compression causes progressive visual-field loss in 30-79%; the affected pathway is central.

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive visual-field defects in 30-79% reflect compression of the optic chiasm, a central nervous system structure.
decisions.ocular: none: the field loss is caused by chiasmal compression; direct injury to the eye or prechiasmal optic nerve is not established.

basis: The definition explicitly identifies an organic brain syndrome following substance reduction. Other withdrawal symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: explicitly defined as an organic brain syndrome, so this is neurologic dysfunction rather than a purely psychiatric substance-use diagnosis.

basis: Blistering and scarring of skin and mucous membranes define DEB, including oral mucosa. Severe esophageal injury varies by subtype and is not assumed across the umbrella.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal blistering and scarring belong to the defining mucocutaneous disease; severe esophageal disease is not required.

basis: Severe intellectual, speech and motor developmental impairment define the disease. Short distal phalanges in 4/9 are dysmorphic, without demonstrated skeletal dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short distal phalanges occur in 4/9, but frequency alone does not establish functional skeletal damage; hypotonia and ambulation defects are neurologic.

basis: ACTH/cortisol excess causes bone loss/myopathy, skin atrophy and secondary hypertension, each 30-79%. Endogenous immunodeficiency (30-79%) is omitted at the four-organ cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: secondary hypertension (30-79%) is a direct manifestation of cortisol excess; no later cardiovascular complications are inferred.
decisions.infectious_immune: none under cap: endogenous immunodeficiency is reported in 30-79%, but bone/muscle, skin and cardiovascular damage take priority.

basis: Defining seizures (7/15) and lung disease with hemorrhage (6/15); hepatic injury in 12/15. Hemophagocytosis (6/15) omitted at cap; renal insufficiency is 4/15.

decisions.haematologic: none under cap: hemophagocytosis in 6/15 supports blood involvement, but frequent hepatic injury, defining seizures and severe pulmonary hemorrhage take priority.
decisions.pulmonary: primary: lung disease is explicitly defining, with direct pulmonary hemorrhage in 6/15 (40%).
decisions.neurologic: primary: early-onset seizures are explicitly defining and occur in 7/15 (47%); this is not inferred from infection risk alone.

basis: Marrow failure; limb reduction, renal agenesis and auditory canal atresia each reported in 1/1. Palatal, cardiac and eyelid defects omitted at cap; single-case frequencies are uncertain.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: bilateral cleft palate is reported in 1/1, but severe limb defects, absent kidney and auditory canal atresia take priority.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal atresia/stenosis in 1/1 represents structural obstruction with expected hearing impairment; evidence is limited to one case.

basis: Nematode infection; sustained larval occupation and inflammation of subcutis occur in most patients (>30%). CNS, ocular and pulmonary invasion are minority manifestations.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous/subcutaneous larval migration causes direct tissue inflammation in most cases; it is a common manifestation of the broader infection.
